dimensions.name: Requirements and scope
dimensions.description: Clarifies functional and non-functional requirements, states assumptions, and identifies what is out of scope.

levels.1: Restates the prompt without clarifying scope or assumptions.
levels.2: Lists the main features but misses availability, latency, or retention expectations.
levels.3: Separates functional and non-functional requirements and states the important assumptions.
levels.4: Also identifies ambiguous requirements, proposes concrete targets, and explains which trade-offs the targets imply.

dimensions.name: API design
dimensions.description: Defines the create, redirect, delete, and analytics interfaces, including errors and idempotency.

levels.1: No clear API or only a vague create-link call.
levels.2: Defines the main endpoints but omits error cases, auth, or response shapes.
levels.3: Defines request and response shapes, status codes, and the main error cases.
levels.4: Also covers idempotency, rate limits, custom aliases, expiry semantics, and how clients discover short links.

dimensions.name: Data model and storage
dimensions.description: Chooses entities, keys, indexes, and a storage engine that fit the access pattern.

levels.1: No data model or an unusable one-to-one table.
levels.2: Has a mapping table but does not justify the key or storage engine.
levels.3: Defines the mapping and analytics schemas with keys and indexes that match the read path.
levels.4: Also discusses sharding, hot keys, retention, and how the model evolves for custom aliases and expiry.

dimensions.name: High-level architecture
dimensions.description: Separates the read and write paths and places caches, queues, and datastores sensibly.

levels.1: A single box with no separation of components.
levels.2: Names services or datastores but does not show how requests flow.
levels.3: Shows a clear read path, write path, and the role of the cache and analytics pipeline.
levels.4: Also explains why each boundary exists, how components scale independently, and what happens during partial failure.

dimensions.name: Scale and performance
dimensions.description: Sizes the system against the stated traffic and explains how each tier scales.

levels.2: Repeats the numbers without estimating storage, QPS, or cache size.
levels.3: Estimates storage and per-tier QPS and describes horizontal scaling for the hot path.
levels.4: Also quantifies cache hit rate, tail latency, replication lag, and the cost of the proposed capacity.

dimensions.name: Trade-offs
dimensions.description: Names the important choices and defends them against at least one alternative.

levels.2: Mentions one trade-off without connecting it to the design.
levels.3: Compares at least two meaningful alternatives, such as SQL vs key-value storage or cache-aside vs write-through.
levels.4: Also explains the conditions under which the chosen option would be wrong and how to revisit the decision.

dimensions.name: Failure modes and operations
dimensions.description: Covers what breaks, how it is detected, and how the system recovers.

levels.2: Mentions replication or backups without a recovery path.
levels.3: Identifies the main failure modes and the metrics or alerts that detect them.
levels.4: Also covers degraded modes, cache or queue outages, poison links, abuse handling, and runbook-level recovery steps.
